subject: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC - sponsorship request
messages:
From: Diana Park <diana@medsafe.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsafe.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We’re preparing a two-week internal zero-trust evaluation and want to run it in an isolated VPC. Because this will touch patient metadata and PHI-derived tokens, our legal and security folks require a short audit window and vendor evidence before we start.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood sponsor pilot credits for a private/VPC POC (estimated $8–12k) so we can cover GPU runtime during the evaluation?
- Would you accept our minimal security packet (SOC2 snapshot + architecture diagram + retention policy) in lieu of the full security review to unblock scheduling next week?

We’re on a tight timeline — ideally start the week of Sep 15. Procurement will handle any paperwork once terms are agreed. Attached is a short worksheet with expected traffic and data types.

Thanks,
Diana Park
Head of Product, Medsafe AI
D: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: zero_trust_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Diana Park <diana@medsafe.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 17:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC

Hi Diana — thanks for the clear ask and the worksheet. Looping in Ben for the commercial side and Jonas for security acceptance. A few quick clarifications so we can move fast:

1) Can you confirm whether the data will be encrypted at rest by your side and whether any cleartext PHI will be uploaded to Redwood?
2) Is the architecture diagram referred to the network topology only, or will it include data flow and anonymization steps?
3) If we agree to sponsor credits, do you need them applied to a Redwood account or a shadow billing/project for procurement?

We’ve historically approved pilot credits for security-gated POCs when a SOC2 in-scope snapshot and a short checklist are provided. Ben — do you have headroom in the promo pool for a 30–60 day commitment? Jonas — any initial guardrails we should require?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC

Sofia / Ben — quick security notes from my side:

- SOC2 snapshot is acceptable as "evidence-in-lieu" for an initial pilot, but we need the latest Type II template or equivalent (PDF).
- We require an architecture diagram that calls out: VPC peering (or dedicated nodes), ingress/egress controls, data-at-rest encryption, key management, and retention windows.
- Please confirm whether PHI will be tokenized before it reaches our runtime. If cleartext PHI is processed, we’ll need an SLA acknowledgement for incident response and a short authorization form signed by procurement.
- Suggested gating checklist (minimal): SOC2 snapshot, diagram, data classification, retention policy, and a named admin contact at Medsafe for the pilot.

If those items are in place, I’m comfortable recommending limited promotional credits conditioned on a 60-day trial window and a short post-trial evidence handoff.

Jonas Weber
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC

Sofia / Jonas — commercial POV:

We can offer a promotional credit package of $10,000 applied to a private/VPC pilot project with these constraints: 1) 60-day validity from activation, 2) usage caps at 120M tokens or equivalent GPU-hours (whichever comes first), 3) pilot is for evaluation only (no production SLA).

I’ll submit for finance approval but want to get the security checklist confirmed first. If Procurement accepts a short MSA amendment that points to our standard pilot terms (see attached draft), we can tie the promo to DEAL-9812 and issue a promo code.

Attachments: promo_credit_terms.pdf

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Diana Park <diana@medsafe.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 13:33:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust pilot credits for private POC - sponsorship approved (conditional)

Hi Diana — quick summary and next steps (approved in principle):

- Approval: Redwood will provide $10,000 in promotional credits for a private/VPC pilot, valid for 60 days from activation. Promo will be tied to DEAL-9812 and project "medsafe-ztp-eval".
- Conditions before activation: delivery of SOC2 Type II snapshot (PDF), architecture diagram including KMS details, named admin contact, and acceptance of the pilot terms (promo_credit_terms.pdf).
- Technical gating: if any cleartext PHI must be processed, Medsafe must confirm tokenization plan or sign the incident response acknowledgement.
- Next actions for Medsafe: send the SOC2 snapshot and diagram to security@redwood.com and confirm procurement contact for the MSA amendment.

I’ve copied Logan from Finance to help turn the promo into an activation token once security signs off. Ben — please forward the promo terms to procurement. Jonas — flag anything you want added to the checklist. Diana — if you can get the packet to us by EOD Friday (Sep 12), we should be able to activate before Sep 18.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
